title: Colors, sizes, and trying on clothes
title_target: สีอะไร ไซส์ไหน — Sǐi à-rai, sái nǎi
goal: Name colors and sizes, ask to try clothes on, say something is too small or too big, and exchange items — while using adjectives that stand after the noun they describe.

dialogs.title: บทสนทนา — At a clothing shop, second floor
dialogs.intro: Budi is looking for a shirt for a meeting. Watch the order of adjectives: colors and sizes always stand **after** the thing they describe, the reverse of English.

lines.speaker: พนักงาน:
lines.text: [หา|Hǎa][อะไร|à-rai][อยู่|yùu][คะ|khá]

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [หา|Hǎa][เสื้อเชิ้ต|sûuea-chóoet][ครับ|khráp] [มี|Mii][สี|sǐi][ขาว|khǎao][ไหม|mǎi][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: A shirt. Do you have any in white?

lines.speaker: พนักงาน:
lines.text: [มี|Mii][ค่ะ|khâ] [ใส่|Sài][ไซส์|sái][อะไร|à-rai][คะ|khá]

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ไม่|Mâi][แน่ใจ|nâae-jai][ครับ|khráp] [ที่|Thîi][อินโดนีเซีย|In-doo-nii-sia][ใส่|sài][แอล|aae-o][ครับ|khráp]

lines.text: [ที่|Thîi][ไทย|thai][ไซส์|sái][เล็ก|lék][กว่า|kwàa][ค่ะ|khâ] [ลอง|Laawng][เอ็กซ์แอล|ék-aae-o][ดู|duu][ไหม|mǎi][คะ|khá]

lines.literal: at — Thai — size — small — more — (polite). try — XL — see — (question) — (polite)?

lines.text: [ลอง|Laawng][ได้|dâai][ไหม|mǎi][ครับ|khráp] [ห้องลอง|Hâwng-laawng][อยู่|yùu][ไหน|nǎi][ครับ|khráp]

lines.text: [ตัว|Tua][นี้|níi][แขน|khǎaen][ยาว|yaao][ไป|pai][หน่อย|nàwy][ครับ|khráp] [มี|Mii][แขนสั้น|khǎaen-sân][ไหม|mǎi][ครับ|khráp]

lines.text: [เอา|Ao][ตัว|tua][นี้|níi][ครับ|khráp] [ถ้า|Thâa][ไม่|mâi][พอดี|phaw-dii][เปลี่ยน|plìan][ได้|dâai][ไหม|mǎi][ครับ|khráp]

lines.literal: take — (classifier) — this — (polite). if — not — fit — exchange — can — (question) — (polite)?

lines.text: [ได้|Dâai][ค่ะ|khâ] [ภายใน|Phaai-nai][เจ็ด|jèt][วัน|wan][ค่ะ|khâ] [เก็บ|Kèp][ใบเสร็จ|bai-sèt][ไว้|wái][นะ|ná][คะ|khá]

lines.literal: can — (polite). within — seven — day — (polite). keep — receipt — put-away — okay — (polite).

notes: **สี sǐi means "color", and it stands IN FRONT of the color name**: *สีขาว* (white), *สีแดง* (red). When attached to an object, the whole cluster moves behind it: *เสื้อสีขาว* (a white shirt — literally "shirt color white"). ⚠️ This order is the reverse of English.

**Thai adjectives always stand AFTER the noun**: *เสื้อใหญ่* (big shirt — literally "shirt big"), *ห้องเล็ก* (small room). Once you get used to it, the order feels logical: first the thing, then what it's like.

**…ไป pai after an adjective means "too".** *ใหญ่ไป* (too big), *แพงไป* (too expensive), *ยาวไป* (too long). Adding *หน่อย nàwy* at the end softens it to "a bit too": *ยาวไปหน่อย* (a bit too long) — and this is the politest form when turning down an item in a shop.

**ลอง laawng means "to try", and is often followed by ดู duu (look).** *ลองดู* = give it a try. *ลองใส่ดู* = try it on. The pattern *verb + ดู* means "try …-ing" for many verbs: *ชิมดู chim duu* (try a taste), *ถามดู thǎam duu* (try asking).
**พอดี phaw-dii means "just right, fits" — and it's used constantly outside clothing too.** *พอดีเลย* = what luck, perfect timing. The word *พอ phaw* alone means enough.

**หมด mòt means "used up, sold out".** *สีขาวหมด* (white is sold out), *เงินหมด* (the money's run out), *หมดแล้ว* (all gone). It also forms *ทั้งหมด tháng-mòt* (all of it), which you've been using since unit 3.

**ไซส์ sái is borrowed from English *size*.** Letter sizes are used as is: *เอส S, เอ็ม M, แอล L, เอ็กซ์แอล XL*. ⚠️ Note the clerk's warning — Thai sizes really do run **one size smaller** than Western sizes for the same brand.
**ถ้า thâa means "if", and it goes at the start of the clause.** *ถ้าไม่พอดี เปลี่ยนได้ไหม* (if it doesn't fit, can I exchange it?). You'll use this pattern constantly from now on.

grammars.title: Twelve colors
after: Some Thai color names are pictures of things, just like English "orange": *สีส้ม* from the orange fruit (*ส้ม*), *สีน้ำตาล* from palm sugar (*น้ำตาล*), *สีฟ้า* from the sky (*ฟ้า*), *สีชมพู* from the name of the rose apple fruit.

⚠️ **สีฟ้า and สีน้ำเงิน are both "blue" but can't be swapped**: the first is light blue like the sky, the second is dark blue. Thai treats them as genuinely different colors, not shades of the same one.

after: ⚠️ **เปลี่ยน *plìan* (exchange for another item) is different from คืน *khuuen* (return for a refund).** In Thailand the first is widely accepted; the second is rare, and at markets almost never. Ask before you pay, not after.

blocks.text: Notice **คู่ khûu** for things that come in pairs (shoes, socks) — the same word also means "partner" in the romantic sense. And **ผ้า phâa** (cloth) forms many words: *ผ้าเช็ดตัว phâa-chét-tua* (towel), *ผ้าปูที่นอน* (bedsheet), *ผ้าห่ม phâa-hòm* (blanket).

blocks.title: Dressing in Thailand: three practical points
items: **Temples require covered shoulders and knees** — for men and women alike. Some big temples rent out cloth wraps, but the lines are long. Keeping a thin long-sleeved shirt in your bag solves this once and for all.
**Thai offices are generally smarter than newcomers expect** — collared shirts are standard, and on Mondays many people wear yellow (Monday's color, see unit 8).
**Indoor AC is very cold** even when it's 35 degrees outside. Cinemas, intercity buses, and office buildings almost always leave people shivering. A word you'll say often: *หนาว nǎao* (cold).

blocks.title: Giving compliments the right way
items: **สวยจัง *sǔai jang*** — so pretty. Used for things and people; for people, usually for women.
**เท่จัง *thêe jang*** — so cool. Better suited to men and to things like watches or motorbikes.
**น่ารัก *nâa-rák*** — cute, lovely. This word is used very widely in Thailand — for children, animals, objects, even adults — and is almost always received as a warm compliment.
⚠️ The **น่า- *nâa-*** pattern forms many adjectives: *น่ากิน* (appetizing), *น่าสนใจ* (interesting), *น่าเบื่อ* (boring), *น่ากลัว* (scary). Literally "worth …-ing".
